title: Scaled Caldeira-Leggett Dynamics: Deterministic Trajectories and the Classical Limit
abstract: The dynamics of an open quantum system in the high-temperature regime of the Caldeira-Leggett model using a Bohmian language is investigated. By expressing the density matrix in polar form, generalized continuity and Hamilton-Jacobi equations are obtained. Thermal effects appear explicitly in the former, while they influence the latter only indirectly through an effective potential. Remarkably, the effective potential does not vanish in the classical limit and cannot, in general, be decomposed into simple additive quantum and thermal contributions. Instead, it retains a nontrivial structure leading to a residual temperature dependence in the resulting dynamics. As a consequence, the resulting temperature-dependent-classical trajectories remain deterministic even in the presence of a thermal environment. This behavior contrasts with the stochastic dynamics observed in the Langevin description and reflects the ensemble-based nature of the present approach. To further explore the quantum-to-classical transition, a scaled version of the Caldeira-Leggett equation is introduced by scaling both the density matrix and Planck constant through a quantumness parameter. This parameter takes the value one in the fully quantum regime and smoothly approaches zero in the classical limit. Applications to Gaussian states demonstrate a gradual suppression of coherence and interference, governed jointly by thermal effects and the transition parameter.
summary: This paper analyzes the transition from quantum to classical behavior in an open system using the Caldeira-Leggett model. By reformulating dynamics in a Bohmian language and introducing a scaling parameter, the authors demonstrate that thermal effects lead to deterministic trajectories rather than stochastic noise at the level of the effective potential. This offers a unified view of dissipation and decoherence across quantum regimes.
main_problem: The paper investigates the quantum-to-classical transition (QCT) for an open quantum system governed by the Caldeira-Leggett model in a thermal environment.
main_result: It shows that the resulting dynamics remain deterministic even with thermal fluctuations, contrasting with stochastic Langevin descriptions, due to a residual structure in the effective potential.
method: The analysis uses a Bohmian language by expressing the density matrix in polar form and deriving coupled generalized Hamilton-Jacobi and continuity equations. A scaled theory approach is employed to study the transition continuously.
model_or_system: The system is an open quantum system interacting with a harmonic bath, modeled via the Caldeira-Leggett (CL) equation. The dynamics are analyzed in the high-temperature limit using a scaling parameter ($\epsilon$) that controls the approach to classicality.
key_observables: Coherence loss (quantified by $\ell_1$-norm), effective potential ($Q$), and deterministic trajectories for phase/amplitude evolution.
important_parameters: Quantumness parameter ($\epsilon$ or $\hbar$), Temperature, Dissipation coefficient ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the high-temperature Ohmic CL model. The derivation of the scaled theory requires specific mathematical extensions not explicitly derived within the framework.
figures_summary: Not specified in notes; focuses on deriving equations and analyzing functional dependencies rather than summarizing figure content.
paper_structure: The paper develops the dynamics using polar decomposition, derives coupled HJ/continuity equations, introduces a scaling parameter ($\epsilon$), analyzes the effective potential's structure across regimes, and contrasts the deterministic results with stochastic expectations.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding how thermal environments modify quantum trajectories during the QCT, offering insights beyond standard Markovian or purely quantum descriptions relevant to open quantum systems.
